lines: Morgan Patel
+1 (555) 010-4410 | morgan.patel@example.com | example.com/code/mpatel
EDUCATION
Ridgeway University | Ph.D. candidate in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2021 - Expected May 2026
Ridgeway University | B.S. in Mathematics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Sunrise Bakery | Assistant Store Manager | Metro City, USA | Sep 2025 - Present
- Managed opening shifts and a team of 6 bakers and cashiers, keeping the store within its weekly labour budget.
- Ran daily stock counts and supplier orders, cutting unsold bread from 12% to 7% of production.
Northpeak Capital | Quantitative Research Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Aug 2025
- Improved risk-adjusted returns by 35% with a cost-aware position smoother on the desk's futures signal.
- Validated the signal on 6 years of tick data with purged walk-forward splits and an embargo period, so every backtest decision used only information available at the time.
- Wrote a feature store for 120 microstructure features with point-in-time joins, which the research team reused in two later signal projects.
- Presented the signal, its capacity estimate and failure cases to the portfolio managers, who approved a small live allocation for the next quarter.
- Selected the smoother's parameters from 400 backtested configurations and reported the best one's Sharpe as the expected live Sharpe.
- Built a short-horizon order-book imbalance signal for liquid index futures that raised the desk book's Sharpe ratio from 1.1 to 1.5 over 18 months of out-of-sample backtest after costs.
Ridgeway University | Research Assistant, Statistical Learning Lab | Metro City, USA | Jun 2020 - Aug 2021
- Cut a 2,000-run Monte Carlo study from 3 days to 5 hours by running the runs in parallel with the same random seed on every worker.
- Derived a variance bound for a sparse regression estimator; my proof tightens the previous bound by a log factor and is now Section 3 of a paper under review at JASA.
- Taught weekly recitations for 60 students in graduate probability, writing 12 problem sets and earning a 4.8/5 teaching rating.
- Released an open-source R package for high-dimensional covariance estimation with shrinkage and factor models, downloaded 3,000 times in its first year.
PROJECTS
Volatility Forecasting Study | Independent Research | Python, PyTorch | Jan 2024 - Present
- Beat a HAR-RV baseline's out-of-sample QLIKE loss by 7% on 30 equity indices with a temporal convolutional model trained on realized-volatility features.
- Tested significance with Diebold-Mariano tests across the 30 indices; after a Holm correction the forecast gain held at the 5% level on 24 of them and in both crisis periods.
- Wrote up the method, robustness checks and results as a 12-page working paper, which was presented at the department's financial econometrics seminar.
Kaggle Market Prediction Competition | Team of 3 | Python | Mar 2023 - Jun 2023
- Engineered features and trained gradient-boosting models for a market prediction competition.
- Cut validation leakage by switching to time-grouped folds, which closed a 0.02 gap between local validation and leaderboard scores.
- Added 0.4 to the Sharpe ratio of a futures book with an order-book imbalance signal, tested over 18 months out of sample.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, R, PyTorch, Kafka
Methods: time-series econometircs, high-dimensional statistics, gradient boosting

items.says: Verify that the code link leads to a real, polished portfolio with relevant research, packages, experiments, or technical writing.
items.because: An empty or generic repository can hurt more than having no link.

items.says: Add a location or work-authorization signal if relevant to the target market.
items.because: Finance employers may recruit by office or require specific authorization.

items.says: Consider adding a LinkedIn profile only if it is complete and consistent with the résumé.
items.because: An incomplete profile creates an avoidable credibility issue.

items.says: Add the Ph.D. research area or dissertation topic.
items.because: “Ph.D. candidate in Statistics” is broad and does not identify the relevant specialty.

items.says: Make the Ph.D. candidacy status and availability for the target role unambiguous.
items.because: The expected date alone does not fully clarify availability.

items.says: Add a small number of highly relevant courses if they strengthen the target.
items.because: Courses such as time series, stochastic processes, optimization, numerical methods, or financial econometrics could reinforce the quant profile.

items.says: Include the advisor, dissertation title, or research group if meaningful for the role.
items.because: These details can help for research-heavy quant positions.

items.says: Reduce the visual emphasis on the B.S. relative to the Ph.D.
items.because: The graduate training is the more important signal for the target role.

items.says: Consider removing the B.S. if space is needed.
items.because: It is no longer essential near completion of a Ph.D. unless it provides a useful signal.

items.says: The résumé lacks a concise target-oriented summary covering Ph.D. status, quant target, technical strengths, market experience, and key credibility signals.
items.because: Recruiters currently have to infer the target and may misclassify the candidate.

items.says: The recent bakery role is positioned above the much more relevant quantitative internship and university research.
items.because: A recruiter may assume store management is the current professional direction.

items.says: The volatility forecasting project should receive more prominence, potentially immediately after Northpeak.
items.because: It is strong evidence for systematic research roles.

items.says: Reorder the Northpeak bullets into a coherent story led by the strongest credible signal result and validation evidence.
items.because: The current order includes technically ambiguous material among the strongest accomplishments.

items.says: Move the open-source package bullet ahead of the teaching bullet in the university research entry.
items.because: Software development, public delivery, and adoption are stronger quant credentials than teaching.

items.says: Make the scale and ownership of the shift-management responsibilities clearer.
items.because: The bullet combines shift management, team supervision, and budget control without showing the degree of responsibility or result.

items.says: Add the budget size, savings, or another measurable operational outcome if available.
items.because: Staying within budget is a baseline expectation without evidence of scale or improvement.

items.says: Clarify whether the six employees were directly supervised or merely coordinated.
items.because: The distinction matters for leadership credibility.

items.says: Explain the operational mechanism that reduced unsold bread from 12% to 7%.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether the improvement came from forecasting, order timing, production changes, or supplier coordination.

items.says: Specify what metric “risk-adjusted returns” represents.
items.because: A technical reader needs to know whether it means Sharpe ratio, information ratio, return per unit of volatility, or another measure.

items.says: Clarify the comparison period, universe, transaction-cost assumptions, and baseline behind the 35% figure.
items.because: Without this context, the improvement is difficult to evaluate and may appear inflated.

items.says: Reconcile the 35% improvement with the later increase in Sharpe from 1.1 to 1.5.
items.because: The figures may be consistent, but their relationship is not obvious.

items.says: Identify the individual contribution to the position smoother.
items.because: “Improved” can imply ownership of the entire strategy rather than work on the desk’s existing signal.

items.says: State whether the validation covered the smoother, the signal, the full strategy, or the research pipeline.
items.because: The object being validated is currently unclear.

items.says: Clarify the embargo interval and why it was chosen if it was methodologically meaningful.
items.because: A quant interviewer may ask what was embargoed and why.

items.says: Specify the feature store’s implementation and engineering scope, including areas such as versioning, storage, latency, testing, or deployment.
items.because: Quant development reviewers will want more than the statement that a feature store was written.

items.says: Clarify whether later projects reused the infrastructure, the 120 features, or both.
items.because: “Reused in two later signal projects” is ambiguous.

items.says: Clarify the candidate’s role in the live-allocation decision.
items.because: The bullet should not imply that the intern managed capital or made the final investment decision.

items.says: Add the scale or risk limits of the live allocation if permitted.
items.because: A “small” allocation is otherwise difficult to interpret.

items.says: Identify the failure cases that were presented.
items.because: The current wording leaves the failure-mode analysis underdeveloped.

items.says: The best Sharpe selected from 400 backtested configurations is incorrectly reported as the expected live Sharpe.
items.because: This is a classic multiple-testing and selection-bias problem without an independent holdout, nested validation, or another defensible procedure.

items.says: The order-book imbalance signal and 18-month Sharpe result appear to duplicate the Kaggle claim.
items.because: The duplication creates uncertainty about where the work was done and whether the result is being double-counted.

items.says: Clarify what “the desk book” means.
items.because: It could refer to an existing portfolio, a simulated book, or a research portfolio.

items.says: Clarify whether the 18-month out-of-sample period was untouched during model selection and accounted for slippage, capacity constraints, and changing market regimes.
items.because: The backtest methodology is underspecified.

items.says: Add constraints or supporting diagnostics rather than presenting the Sharpe increase alone as evidence of production readiness.
items.because: A Sharpe increase by itself does not establish production readiness.

items.says: Using the same random seed on every worker can create identical or correlated random streams.
items.because: Duplicated random streams would undermine the Monte Carlo simulation.

items.says: State whether independent reproducible streams or separate worker seeds were used.
items.because: Reproducibility is positive, but duplicated streams are not.

items.says: Add the parallel-computing implementation environment if relevant.
items.because: Vectorization, cluster execution, or job scheduling can be useful signals for quant research roles.

items.says: Make the authorship role precise by identifying whether the candidate is first author, coauthor, or contributor.
items.because: “My proof” may overstate the candidate’s role.

items.says: State the manuscript status with exact terminology and avoid implying acceptance.
items.because: Under review, submitted, revise-and-resubmit, accepted, and published have materially different credibility.

items.says: Identify the source and scale of the 4.8/5 teaching rating.
items.because: The rating is useful only if its legitimacy is clear.

items.says: Clarify whether the candidate designed the course materials or only delivered assigned recitations.
items.because: This determines the level of ownership.

items.says: Clarify whether the 3,000 downloads were measured through CRAN, GitHub, or another source.
items.because: Different download sources carry different meanings.

items.says: Add quality evidence such as tests, documentation, continuous integration, external contributors, or research use.
items.because: This would strengthen the package claim.

items.says: Include the package name or a link if it is publicly available and polished.
items.because: It would substantiate the technical claims.

items.says: Make the candidate’s ownership or contribution to the software package precise.
items.because: Several claims currently leave project ownership ambiguous.

items.says: Clarify the data period and forecast horizon.
items.because: Both materially affect interpretation of the 7% improvement.

items.says: Specify whether the evaluation was fully out of sample and how hyperparameters were selected.
items.because: The current wording does not establish that the comparison was fair.

items.says: Explain why a temporal convolutional model was appropriate if space allows.
items.because: The résumé should show the methodological reasoning.

items.says: Clarify the unit or structure of the 5% significance result.
items.because: It is unclear whether tests were performed separately by index, across horizons, or in another structure.

items.says: State whether the crisis-period analysis was pre-specified or selected after examining the data.
items.because: This affects the credibility of the robustness claim.

items.says: Keep the statistical-test detail subordinate to the practical forecasting result.
items.because: The bullet should support the forecasting claim rather than read like a methods appendix.

items.says: Clarify that the working paper is not a publication.
items.because: The paper’s status should not be mistaken for publication.

items.says: Add a link to the paper or presentation if available.
items.because: A technical reviewer may want to inspect the methodology.

items.says: State whether the candidate was the sole author or part of a team.
items.because: Ownership is important for evaluating the project.

items.says: Add the competition result, performance, or ranking, or remove the bullet.
items.because: The bullet currently lists activities without a concrete technical outcome.

items.says: Specify the dataset or prediction task if it helps establish relevance.
items.because: Generic competition language does not differentiate the candidate.

items.says: Explain the leakage mechanism and the resulting validation design.
items.because: This is needed to demonstrate understanding of temporal validation.

items.says: Clarify whether closing the 0.02 gap reduced overestimation, improved leaderboard performance, or both.
items.because: Closing a validation-leaderboard gap is not automatically a positive result without context.

items.says: The futures-book Sharpe claim appears to duplicate Northpeak’s order-book imbalance result.
items.because: The same signal concept, 18-month period, and performance change make the résumé look padded and potentially double-counted.

items.says: If this was a separate experiment, distinguish its dataset, signal, period, and portfolio construction from Northpeak.
items.because: The two results are otherwise not sufficiently differentiated.

items.says: Do not call it a “futures book” if it was only a simulated competition portfolio.
items.because: The terminology should accurately reflect the environment and ownership.

items.says: Show how the listed programming tools were used in the experience bullets.
items.because: The résumé does not provide enough evidence for each listed technology.

items.says: Remove Kafka unless it was used meaningfully or add supporting experience.
items.because: The unsupported entry can look like keyword stuffing.

items.says: Add relevant data and research tooling such as SQL, version control, testing, numerical libraries, distributed computing, databases, or cluster tooling if accurate.
items.because: The skills section is insufficiently specific for research and production-quality workflows.

items.says: Separate research languages from production or infrastructure tools.
items.because: This would make the technical profile easier to understand.

items.says: “Econometircs” is misspelled and should be “econometrics.”
items.because: A spelling error in a core target-domain skill is especially damaging.

items.says: Use consistent, conventional names for the methods listed.
items.because: The terminology should align with the projects and publications.

items.says: Add methods already demonstrated by the résumé, such as point-in-time validation, walk-forward testing, multiple-testing correction, volatility forecasting, microstructure features, Monte Carlo simulation, and statistical inference.
items.because: The current methods list understates the demonstrated expertise.
